The '''1999–2000''' season of the [[Belgian First Division A|Jupiler League]] was held between August 6, 1999, and May 11, 2000.  [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Sporting Anderlecht]] became champions.

These teams were promoted from the [[Belgian Second Division|second division]] at the start of the season:
*[[Y.R. K.V. Mechelen|KV Mechelen]] (second division champions)
*[[K.F.C. Verbroedering Geel|Verbroedering Geel]] (playoff winner)

==Relegated teams==
These teams were relegated to the second division at the end of the season:
*[[K.F.C. Verbroedering Geel|Verbroedering Geel]]
*[[K.F.C. Lommel S.K.|Lommel]]

==Anderlecht's title success==
Anderlecht became champions on April 21, 2000, after the defeat of rival [[Club Brugge]] at [[Herman Vanderpoortenstadion]] to [[Lierse S.K. (1906)|Lierse]] 1-0 as, prior to these results, they were 7 points ahead of Brugge with 3 matches to go.  The next day Anderlecht beat [[K.R.C. Genk|Racing Genk]] 4-1 and then [[Standard Liège]] 2-0.

==Battle for Europe==
Club Brugge and [[K.A.A. Gent|Gent]] qualified for the [[UEFA Cup]].

==The relegation dog fight==
[[R. Charleroi S.C.|Charleroi]] avoided relegation with a controversial draw against Anderlecht on the last day of the season.  Anderlecht were already champions and played with [[Enzo Scifo]] who had previously signed a deal with Charleroi.  However, the result was irrelevant as Geel lost their last match to Club Brugge and were thus relegated with Lommel.
